title: Neural uncertainty flags difficult dopamine transporter scans
summary: Residual-network ensembles classified dopamine-transporter SPECT and flagged uncertain decisions. A separate 645-scan Parkinson progression dataset showed 98.0% binary classification accuracy against clinical diagnosis; the uncertainty module flagged 92.3% of classification errors. Performance varied across camera datasets. This retrospective evaluation does not establish improved patient management or reliable exclusion of neurodegeneration in individual borderline scans.
organization: University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf; Jung Diagnostics

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Development on 1,250 scans, separate 490-scan development test, 640-scan camera test, and 645-scan external clinical-reference test.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical utility remains unestablished; reference labels differ across cohorts, camera shifts affect performance, and uncertainty is binary rather than a calibrated probability.
evidence.ai_role: Separate high-sensitivity and high-specificity learned ensembles flag disagreement around an independently generated image classification.
